description: REQ-105's seeded `citizens.json` stores each citizen's `telemetryPath` as a template string containing a literal, unresolved `$HOME` placeholder, e.g. `"telemetryPath": "$HOME/.automaton/state/telemetry.json"` (behavioral-spec.md:375). REQ-101's Edge Cases rely on this exact field to locate 'its own most-recently-read liquid balance (read from its own `state/telemetry.json`, located via REQ-105's registry `telemetryPath` field...)' (behavioral-spec.md:137-138, 145-146). Unlike the bash scripts this pattern is modeled on (`economy/ubi/run.sh`, where `$HOME` is a real shell variable automatically expanded by the shell before the string ever reaches the script), a JSON file's string value is inert data -- no runtime environment automatically substitutes `$HOME` inside a JSON string field read by, e.g., a Node.js `readCitizenBalances()` module (verification-architecture.md:25). Nowhere does REQ-101, REQ-105, or the Purity Boundary Map specify WHOSE `$HOME` this placeholder should resolve against (the reading/coordinator process's own `$HOME`? a per-citizen `$HOME` value not otherwise present in the registry, see FIND-202?) nor what resolution function performs the substitution. This is a smaller, adjacent instance of the same class of gap as FIND-202: a field's usability depends on an unspecified resolution step.

additionalEvidence.note: REQ-101's own reliance on telemetryPath to locate the balance file, with no resolution mechanism specified
readCitizenBalances() effectful-shell row -- reads telemetryPath directly with no mention of a $HOME-substitution step
